slides.0.title: Hungary's Major White Grape Varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Furmint, Hárslevelű, Olaszrizling and Native Varieties
slides.1.title: Furmint — The King of Hungarian White Grapes
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The Soul of Tokaj
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The principal variety of Tokaji Aszú, accounting for approximately 65–70% of the vineyards in the Tokaj region
slides.1.highlights.1.title: A High-Acid Backbone
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Naturally high acidity (pH 2.9–3.1) gives sweet wines a perfect sweet-acid balance and endows dry wines with outstanding ageing potential
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Thin Skin — Susceptible to Botrytis
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The grape's thin skin is easily penetrated by the botrytis mould — the perfect precondition for producing Aszú berries
slides.1.highlights.3.title: The Dry Revolution
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Since the 21st century, dry Furmint has become Hungary's most important white export wine, showcasing minerality and complexity
slides.1.content:
The name Furmint is thought to derive from the French word "froment" (wheat), a reference to the golden, wheat-like colour of the ripe berries. Today it is recognised as one of the world's great white wine grapes.

Ripening: Late-ripening
Skin: Thin, highly susceptible to botrytis
Acidity: Very high — one of the world's highest-acid white varieties
Key regions: Tokaj · Somló · Badacsony · Eger

Flavour Profile

Young dry: Green apple, lime, white blossom, mineral, high acidity
Aged dry: Honey, apricot, hazelnut, flint, cream
Aszú: Apricot jam, candied orange peel, beeswax, ginger, cinnamon
slides.2.title: Hárslevelű — The Linden Leaf Variety
slides.2.highlights.0.title: What the Name Means
slides.2.highlights.0.content: "Hárslevelű" means "linden leaf" in Hungarian, reflecting the shape of its leaves and its characteristic linden-blossom aroma
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Generous Aromatics
slides.2.highlights.1.content: More aromatic than Furmint, with notes of linden blossom, apricot, lychee and honey
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The Perfect Partner
slides.2.highlights.2.content: In a blend with Furmint, Hárslevelű contributes fragrance while Furmint provides the structure — together they create the complete Aszú style
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Thick-Skinned
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Its thicker skin is more resistant to rot in wet years — the winemaker's "insurance variety" in difficult vintages
slides.2.content:
Hárslevelű is the second most important variety in Tokaj and an essential blending partner for Furmint. Its higher aromatic intensity adds a floral, honeyed dimension that Furmint's structure alone cannot provide.

Furmint vs Hárslevelű

CharacteristicFurmintHárslevelű
AcidityVery highHigh, but lower than Furmint
Skin thicknessThinThicker
Ageing potentialLong — decadesMedium — aromatic complexity
Flavour profileMineral, citrus, appleLinden blossom, apricot, honey

A higher proportion of Hárslevelű in the blend gives a Tokaji Aszú a more floral, honeyed character; a higher Furmint ratio increases backbone and mineral precision.
slides.3.title: Olaszrizling — Hungary's Most Widely Planted White Grape
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The Most Widely Planted Variety
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Hungary's most extensively planted white grape, found in almost all 22 wine regions across the country
slides.3.highlights.1.title: A Central European Favourite
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Known as Welschriesling in Austria and widely grown in Croatia and Slovenia — it is not Rhine Riesling
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The Face of Lake Balaton
slides.3.highlights.2.content: At its best on the northern shore of Lake Balaton, where volcanic soils impart distinctive minerality and good acidity
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Fresh and Approachable Style
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Typically light and fresh — apple, pear and floral notes with moderate acidity — the backbone of everyday Hungarian table wine
slides.3.content:
Despite the name, Olaszrizling has no genetic connection to Rhine Riesling (DNA analysis has confirmed they are entirely different varieties). "Olasz" means Italian in Hungarian, but the grape's true origin is Central European rather than Italian.

Regional Styles

Badacsony (basalt): Strongest mineral character, volcanic tension, most complex
Balatonfüred-Csopak (limestone): Crisp, high-acid, clean and precise
Somló (volcanic basalt): Unique mineral quality with a distinctive volcanic edge
Eger / Mátra (mixed soils): Medium-bodied, fresh everyday style

Two Main Styles

Plains style: Light, crisp, apple-pear, for early drinking
Balaton volcanic style: Mineral, high acidity, complex, age-worthy
slides.4.title: Other Important White Grape Varieties
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Juhfark (Sheep's Tail)
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Almost exclusively grown in the volcanic Somló region, celebrated for its extreme acidity and fierce minerality — traditionally served as the "wedding night wine"
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Szürkebarát (Grey Friar)
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Pinot Gris — produces Hungary's finest expression of the variety on the volcanic soils of the northern Lake Balaton shore
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Irsai Olivér
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Intensely Muscat-scented, early-ripening and widely planted — the gateway variety for many people discovering Hungarian white wine
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Cserszegi Fűszeres
slides.4.highlights.3.content: The name means "spicy" — rose water, lychee and spice aromas; an aromatic variety offering exceptional value for money
slides.4.content:
Hungary is home to dozens of native varieties, many found nowhere else in the world. Here are two standout rarities worth knowing.

Juhfark — "Sheep's Tail"

  • Name refers to the long, tapering shape of the grape cluster
  • Almost exclusively cultivated on the Somló volcano — fewer than 400 bottles per hectare
  • Extreme acidity, powerful mineral character — one of Hungary's most distinctive whites
  • Traditional "wedding night wine" — legend holds it aids conception

Szürkebarát — "Grey Friar" (Pinot Gris)

  • Name derives from the grey colour of the ripe berries and the grey habits of Cistercian monks
  • Best expression on Badacsony's basalt soils: rich, smoky, mineral
  • Fuller-bodied than most Central European Pinot Gris

slides.6.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Why is Furmint the ideal grape for producing Tokaji Aszú?
A. Its thick skin keeps the grapes intact during long hang time
B. Its thin skin is easily penetrated by botrytis, and its high acidity balances the extreme sugar levels
C. It has the lowest acidity of all Hungarian varieties, making the wine soft
D. It is the most cold-hardy variety and well suited to Tokaj's harsh winters

Furmint's thin skin is easily penetrated by Botrytis Cinerea (noble rot), enabling the fungus to dehydrate and concentrate the berries. Its naturally very high acidity then provides the structural counterbalance to the extreme sugar levels — without that acidity, Aszú would taste cloying rather than vibrantly sweet.
What is Hárslevelű's main contribution to a Tokaji Aszú blend?
A. It provides the backbone structure and high acidity
B. It provides aromatic floral richness and roundness to complement Furmint's backbone
C. It adds deep colour to the wine
D. It reduces the overall acidity to make the wine more approachable

Hárslevelű's role in a Tokaji Aszú blend is to provide aromatic complexity — linden blossom, apricot and honey — together with a rounder, fuller texture. Furmint contributes the structural backbone and mineral precision; Hárslevelű adds the fragrant, plush dimension that makes Aszú so seductive.
Are Olaszrizling and Rhine Riesling the same grape variety?
A. Yes — Olaszrizling is simply the Hungarian name for Rhine Riesling
B. No — they are completely different varieties, confirmed by DNA analysis
C. They are closely related sub-varieties of the same parent clone
D. Olaszrizling is an Italian sub-variety of Rhine Riesling

Olaszrizling (also known as Welschriesling in Austria) and Rhine Riesling are entirely distinct varieties — confirmed by DNA profiling. Despite the shared name, they have different flavour profiles, acidity levels and ageing characteristics. In Hungary "Olasz" (meaning "Italian") refers to the variety's perceived foreign origin, not to Rhine Riesling.
What makes Juhfark distinctive among Hungarian white varieties?
A. It is Hungary's most widely planted white variety, grown in every region
B. It grows almost exclusively on the Somló volcano, producing extreme acidity and minerality, and is traditionally known as the "wedding night wine"
C. It is a late-harvested sweet wine variety similar to Furmint
D. It is a synonym for Pinot Gris widely grown around Lake Balaton

Juhfark (meaning "sheep's tail" — after the shape of the cluster) is grown almost exclusively on the volcanic soils of Somló, with yields as low as 400 litres per hectare. Its extreme acidity and fierce minerality make it one of Hungary's most distinctive white wines. Its folk reputation as a fertility aid gave rise to the tradition of serving it as the "wedding night wine."
